channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: Judge extends press access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico
item.description: U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly extended an order preserving White House access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico while their lawsuit proceeds. Kelly, appointed by President Trump, said the outlets are likely to show that restrictions imposed after reporting on a ballroom project amounted to unlawful viewpoint discrimination.

item.title: WordPress 7.1.3 fixes seven security flaws
item.description: WordPress 7.1.3 is a maintenance and security release with seven security fixes and four bug fixes. The patched issues include stored cross-site scripting through pending comments, a denial-of-service flaw, second-order SQL injection in WXR exports and disclosure of private or unpublished comments. Site owners are urged to update promptly.

item.title: Podnews weighs new RSS tags against platform lock-in
item.description: Podnews' weekly review examines Libsyn's proposed RSS namespace for ad-slot availability, newsletters as membership and audience-data products, and the expansion of transcripts and person tags. The discussion keeps returning to a foundational concern for podcasting: open infrastructure versus features that pull creators and listeners into platform lock-in.

item.title: Newsrooms build direct audiences beyond big platforms
item.description: The Reuters Institute reports on independent publishers cooperating to extend their reach while rebuilding direct reader relationships. Examples include a human-curated French news portal, Scotland’s community newsroom network and a Paris culture newsletter that grew to 250,000 subscribers before expanding into print and events.

item.title: W3C advances accessibility, open source and web interoperability
item.description: W3C’s September roundup covers an updated WCAG 3.0 draft, a pilot open-source interoperability program, Web Authentication Level 4 and fresh work on digital-rights policy. It also lists newly cross-browser web features and previews TPAC discussions about improving the standards process and its tools.

item.title: European supercomputer bet leans on open-source ROCm
item.description: French cloud company Scaleway plans a Sweden-based supercomputer using AMD Instinct chips and the open-source ROCm software stack. The project is noteworthy for developers because ROCm supports widely used programming tools without tying applications to Nvidia’s proprietary CUDA ecosystem, offering another path around hardware lock-in.

item.title: Microsoft president calls for global rules on advanced models
item.description: Microsoft president Brad Smith said advanced computing models face fewer safety requirements than ordinary goods such as milk. He urged governments to require independent evaluation, incident reporting, emergency shutdown mechanisms and notice to people harmed by system failures, with Britain's security institute serving as one possible model.

item.title: Hungary's once-dominant newspaper returns online
item.description: Népszabadság, abruptly closed in 2016 after six decades in print, has relaunched as an online publication. Its editor says the revived newsroom will emphasize classic reporting and questioning in a media environment dominated by outlets friendly to Viktor Orbán's government. The return restores a historic independent voice before Hungary's election.

item.title: ATSC advances broadcast-to-everything standard
item.description: ATSC approved a candidate standard for Broadcast-to-Everything, laying groundwork for broadcasters to deliver data and services to connected devices beyond television sets. The milestone opens technical review of an interoperable platform intended to link broadcast infrastructure with wireless networks, device makers and software developers.

item.title: Justice Department probes networks over White House pool boycott
item.description: The Justice Department opened an antitrust inquiry into ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News after the networks collectively stopped White House pool coverage when reporters from CNN, Politico and MS NOW lost credentials. The case turns a press-access dispute into a test of whether coordinated newsroom action can be treated as a commercial group boycott.

item.title: The problem with Facebook was Facebook
item.description: John Herrman argues that years of reform debates mistook Facebook's harms for correctable lapses instead of consequences of its core attention-and-data business. Recommendation systems steadily displaced social connections with optimized, unfamiliar content, while changing corporate missions offered little accountability for the platform's underlying incentives.

item.title: Worker-owned Hell Gate tests a harder membership pitch
item.description: New York local outlet Hell Gate has about 11,000 paid subscriptions and has passed $1 million in annual recurring revenue, but growth has slowed. The worker-owned newsroom is experimenting with occasional limits on free access, sharper membership appeals and events while keeping subscriber support central to its independence.

item.title: LoopConf trades corporate sponsors for attendee funding
item.description: Organizer Brian Richards explains why LoopConf US is relying on early ticket sales instead of corporate sponsorship. The 2027 WordPress developer conference will cap attendance at 100–200 people, use a lightweight static site and emphasize open-source resilience and cross-platform ideas.

item.title: Nieman Lab redesigns 100,000 pages without flattening them
item.description: Joshua Benton details Nieman Lab’s first major redesign in years: more art-directed story layouts, rebuilt archives, improved search and new beats for platforms, creators and local news. Migrating 12,000 articles and more than 100,000 URLs also required preserving a decade of custom CSS and hand-coded publishing history.

item.title: Open source moves to the center of Europe’s digital-sovereignty push
item.description: At Open Source Summit Europe, Linux Foundation leaders argued that Europe’s security and sovereignty policies converge on one practical need: trustworthy software supply chains. Open source can provide auditable, reusable infrastructure while reducing dependence on a few overseas cloud and platform vendors.
